newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Stanley says 49's game has steady start.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Stanley says 49's game has steady start.

text.p: A daily numbers draw introduced by bookmakers last month to compete with the UK National Lottery has made a "steady start", Stanley Leisure chairman Leonard Steinberg said on Wednesday.
"The 49's bet is only four weeks old and has started off steadily and improved over those four weeks," Steinberg told Reuters in an interview.

Steinberg would not be drawn on the revenues from the game which is broadcast live every day in subscribing bettting shops including those run by Ladbroke Plc. Lottery operator Camelot is to launch a midweek draw on February 5.
Steinberg said the game would have to be judged in the light of the increased competition from the National Lottery.
Customers can bet on between one and five numbers and odds range from 11/2 on one number to 99,999/1 for all five.
The average bet placed on the game is only 1.50 stg against an average of 4.57 stg for betting in general, Steinberg said.

Betting shop business has been hit by the cold weather over the past month with most meetings cancelled. But Steinberg said all-weather racing and changes like the introduction of fruit machines meant business continued to run at around 80 percent of normal.

Steinberg said the acquisition of the Gus Carter betting shops was proving a success although the chain had been hit by 340,000 stg restructuring costs and a 543,000 stg pay-out on Frankie Dettori's seven winners at Ascot.
He said that the acquisition should add some 1.8 million stg to annual operating profit once one-off costs were excluded.
Stanley's group pre-tax profit rose 21 percent to 7.4 million stg in the six months to October 27. Earnings per share increased by some 20 percent to 4.51p.
Proposed new legislation would allow casinos to open in 20 areas of England where they are currently prohibited.

Steinberg said Stanley was interested in opening casinos in the Yorkshire city of Harrogate and around London but doubted whether seaside towns such as Morecambe, Weymouth and Hastings, all proposed sites, could support casinos.
